breakthrough: Performance improves while sensitive data stays where it belongs
lane: Technical foundation, resilience, and runtime substrate
outcome: Place data and compute together according to privacy, latency, and transfer cost

phases.name: Phase 1 - Build the Data Locality Optimizer Core

subphases.name: 1.1 Data Locality Optimizer Domain Model and State Plane
work: Define typed entities, capabilities, jobs, events, state transitions, and outputs required to place data and compute together according to privacy, latency, and transfer cost, with explicit versions and validation at every boundary.

Implement an owned persistent state layer optimized for service isolation, configuration, identity, health, compatibility, performance, and platform portability; include snapshots or event history when state changes over time.
Expose create, query, update, subscribe, and delete operations through local APIs plus an SDK that never requires private cross-runtime imports.

subphases.name: 1.2 Data Locality Optimizer Execution Runtime
work: Build resumable workers and state machines that perform the core operation: place data and compute together according to privacy, latency, and transfer cost.
Add cancellation, idempotency, bounded retries, timeouts, quotas, sandbox limits, and deterministic recovery from partial failure.
Create a local simulator that can replay success, malformed inputs, disconnection, overload, provider loss, and restart recovery.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Make Data Locality Optimizer Adaptive and Usable

subphases.name: 2.1 Data Locality Optimizer Decision and Learning Engine
work: Implement scoring, planning, prediction, search, or optimization using resource control, anomaly detection, topology optimization, compatibility analysis, and energy modeling.
Create feedback signals from task outcomes and user corrections; update tunable behavior without silently changing hard safety limits.
Return confidence, alternatives, bottlenecks, and a concise machine-readable explanation for every important automated choice.

subphases.name: 2.2 Data Locality Optimizer Interaction Surface
work: Build the primary experience in the foundation console, live dependency topology, compatibility matrix, and resource heatmap, including live state, controls, errors, and recovery actions.
Add a CLI and typed client library so humans, agents, games, and third-party applications can operate the capability directly.
Stream progress and intermediate artifacts in real time so long operations remain inspectable, interruptible, and steerable.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Scale Data Locality Optimizer into a Breakthrough Product

subphases.name: 3.1 Data Locality Optimizer Offline, Edge, and Cloud Mesh
work: Implement local-only, hybrid, and cloud execution with explicit capability discovery and graceful behavior when optional peers disappear.
Add conflict-safe synchronization, workload placement, caching, backpressure, and failover across devices or nodes where the feature benefits from distribution.
Benchmark latency, throughput, memory, energy, network transfer, and cost; make the scheduler choose the best execution mode from measured constraints.

subphases.name: 3.2 Data Locality Optimizer Signature Breakthrough
work: Implement the differentiating behavior: Performance improves while sensitive data stays where it belongs. Ship it as an opt-in executable mode, not a mockup.
Run adversarial, load, privacy, misuse, degraded-network, and recovery tests against the novel behavior; block unsafe automatic actions.
Package the feature as an independently installable capability with a live demo, sample integration, metrics endpoint, and rollback-safe release artifact.
